title: The denoising MDP, DDPO, and the Diffusion-DPO loss
brief: Treat each step of a tiny diffusion sampler as a Gaussian action, train it toward a reward with DDPO's clipped surrogate, and write the Diffusion-DPO loss for preference pairs.
hints: A trajectory has T + 1 rows: xs[0] is x_T and xs[T] is x_0. Row k of a per-step tensor belongs to diffusion step t = T - k, so index the schedule with t - 1.
ddpm_mean is (x_t - BETAS[t-1] / sqrt(1 - ALPHA_BARS[t-1]) * eps) / sqrt(ALPHAS[t-1]). ALPHAS and ALPHA_BARS are different arrays; mixing them up is the usual bug.
trajectory_logprob must recompute each step's mean from model.eps on the detached states. The ratio in ddpo_loss is exp(logp - logp_old), and the advantages broadcast as advantages[None, :].
In ddpo_train, compute logp_old once per round, under torch.no_grad(), before the epoch loop. Recomputing it inside the loop pins every ratio at 1.
diffusion_dpo_loss is -logsigmoid(-beta * ((err_w - err_w_ref) - (err_l - err_l_ref))), averaged over pairs. Use torch.nn.functional.logsigmoid so large margins stay finite.
